Barry.note:
Accent: British, a plain working-class accent from a town in the south-east of England; not posh, not stagey.
Style: a builder of about fifty in a hi-vis jacket. Blunt, gruff and fed up, short flat sentences, a dry laugh at his own bad luck. Talking to the woman behind the counter, not performing.
Pace: natural, unhurried.

Denise.note:
Accent: British, a working woman from a northern English town; plain and local, not posh.
Style: in her late fifties, owns the café. Dry, tired and quick. Low and level, never raised. She says devastating things as plain sums. Talking to a regular across the counter, not performing.
Pace: natural, quick.

The Ex.note:
Accent: British, privately educated English, a former cabinet minister.
Style: about sixty. Warm, unhurried and reassuring, as if every sentence is a small favour. Never raises his voice. Talking to people round a table, not performing.
Pace: unhurried.

Mr Red.note:
Accent: British, north London, educated.
Style: an English politician of the left in his mid fifties. Earnest and lecturing, pleased with himself. Talking to people round a table, not performing.
Pace: natural.

Mr Red megaphone.note:
Accent: British, north London, educated.
Style: an English politician of the left in his mid fifties, SHOUTING into a megaphone at a protest, furious, self-righteous, full voice, every word hit hard.
Pace: fast and punchy.

Mr Blue megaphone.note:
Accent: British, a Midlands businessman.
Style: an English politician of the right in his mid fifties, SHOUTING into a megaphone at a protest, loud, blunt and indignant, jabbing each word, building up to point at someone.
Pace: fast and punchy.
